title: Residency change scenarios + customer notice templates
content:
Purpose:

This doc is a working reference for eng + legal + CS on how we handle tenant-level data-residency changes: planned region pin migrations, emergency evacuation from a zone, and voluntary customer-requested repinning. It bundles (1) scenario-by-scenario operational steps, (2) minimal evidence artifacts for compliance review, (3) short customer notice templates keyed by severity, and (4) rollback/compensation decision triggers.

Scope:
- Applies to Private deployments and Dedicated tenants where we control region pin assignments.
- Does NOT replace contract/legal wording; use this as an operational complement.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Planned migrations: follow migration play (prepare snapshot, dry-run routing, 72h notice for tiered customers, test acceptance window).
- Emergency evacuations: prioritize evidence capture + soft-notice then full notice. 4-hour operator window to initiate automated snapshot+transfer.
- Customer-initiated repin: support within 5 business days for standard customers, expedited for enterprise with paid migration.

Scenario matrix (short):
- Planned region migration (non-emergency): owner = Eng-PrivateDeploy + CS lead. Steps: announce -> create dry-run environment -> collect residency-evidence bundle -> schedule cutover -> monitor 72h -> close. Risk: medium. Compensation: none unless SLA violated.

- Regulatory enforcement (legal requirement to move out of region): owner = Legal + Eng-PrivateDeploy. Steps: notify customer within 24h, begin accelerated migration, capture signed artifacts for regulator, run post-migration attestation. Risk: high. Compensation: TBD via Legal.

- Emergency capacity or security evacuation: owner = SRE + Eng-PrivateDeploy. Steps: immediate snapshot -> failover to fallback region (if permitted) -> emergency notice -> postmortem and evidence packaging. Risk: critical. Compensation: per SLA.

Operational checklist (working):
- Pre-cutover checklist:
  - Confirm legal constraints (Legal ticket ID present).
  - Confirm model of data movement allowed (encrypted at rest, KMS policy).
  - Create full data snapshot and md5 checksums for top-level partitions.
  - Export tenant-residency-metadata (pin history, consent logs).
  - Dry-run traffic routing against staging anchor (2x traffic for 2h).
  - Prepare rollback snapshot and timeboxed rollback window.

- Cutover checklist:
  - Freeze writes if necessary (announce write freeze window).
  - Execute transfer pipeline (zsync / multi-region rsync pattern).
  - Validate checksums and KV cache priming.
  - Run smoke tests for 10 critical routes (list in linked artifacts).
  - Switch routing policy and gradually increase traffic over 30 minutes.

- Post-cutover:
  - Collect telemetry (latency, error spike, rate limiting).
  - Run residency evidence pack: manifest.json (file list), signed checksums, operator runbook notes, time-stamped commit log.
  - Notify CS + Legal for attestation.

Evidence packaging (minimum for audits):
- Signed manifest of files moved (manifest signed by operator using internal key id).
- Transfer checksums and transfer timestamps.
- Network traces showing egress and ingress endpoints for the window.
- Consent ledger excerpt (if customer-level consent required).
- Internal JIRA/Linear ticket chain + Slack thread permalink.

Telemetry and alerting (must have):
- Route-level latency (>2x baseline) alert.
- Error-rate spike (>1% absolute increase) alert.
- Unexpected geo-origin traffic (>0.5% of daily volume) detection.
- Missing evidence files alert during packaging.

Customer notice templates (short, copyable):
- Planned migration (30–72h):
  Subject: Upcoming region maintenance for your tenant – action required if you restrict data residency
  Body: Hi <CustomerName>,
  We will perform a scheduled migration of your tenant data from <old-region> to <new-region> on <date>. This is to <reason>. No action is required if you’re OK with the move; if you require a different approach (e.g., maintain current region for contract reasons), please reply within 48 hours. We will provide a post-migration attestation bundle.

- Emergency evacuation (immediate):
  Subject: URGENT: Immediate data movement for your tenant due to <security/regulatory event>
  Body: Hi <CustomerName>,
  We are initiating an immediate migration of your tenant to a fallback region to maintain service availability and compliance. Expected window: <start> to <end>. We will share a full evidence package after the migration. Contact <CS Lead> if this conflicts with your policy.

- Successful migration attestation:
  Subject: Migration complete – residency attestation for <tenant id>
  Body: Hi <CustomerName>,
  Migration from <old-region> to <new-region> completed at <timestamp>. Attached: manifest + signed checksums + acceptance tests. Please let us know within 5 business days if anything looks incorrect.

Rollback and compensation triggers (decision heuristics):
- Immediate rollback if critical data integrity failures (checksum mismatch for >0.1% of objects) OR if an unauthorized egress is detected.
- Consider partial rollback (route-level) if latency >3x baseline for >60 minutes and no mitigation available.
- Compensation discussion initiated by CS when SLA latency/window breached or data loss confirmed.

Automation hooks (todo list):
- Automate manifest generation in transfer pipeline (RDW-2199).
- Add evidence-bundler Lambda to post-process artifacts and push to secure S3 for retrieval (conforms with KMS policy).
- Create a smoke-test suite keyed by tenant (tenant-smoke v1).

Links / tickets / refs:
- JIRA: RDW-2199 (artifact bundler), RDW-2244 (migration dry-run infra), RDW-2310 (region-fallback automation)
- Confluence: Residency-standards (internal doc placeholder)
- Slack: #private-deployments (link to thread where we prototyped dry-run)

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Do we need a signed notarization for transfers into EU zones for certain customers? (Legal)
- How do we package model cache artifacts that are large and not file-by-file? (Perf)
- Customer opt-out flow for migration: can we expose a one-click hold in Console? (Product)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider an "attestation-lite" for low-risk customers: checksum + transfer log, no notarization.
- We should keep a small set of legal-ready templates for non-English regions.
- Short-term: run two migrations in staging next sprint (RDW-2244 dry-run) and collect operator timing metrics.

Status: draft. This doc is intentionally operational and contains TODOs. Use linked artifacts for canonical runbooks and legal language.
